lesson_title: Seven Questions, Full Marks: The Chemistry Practice Run
hook_text: One missing line — divide by the volume — and the whole Kc question collapses. Here it is, caught in the act.
clip_script: Concentrations: each entry over 2 cubic decimetres — nitrogen 0,2; hydrogen 0,1; ammonia 0,2 moles per cubic decimetre. One mark, and it is the most forfeited line in the whole calculation: moles poured straight into the constant score nothing past this point. The expression, from the balanced equation: K c equals ammonia concentration squared, over, nitrogen concentration times hydrogen concentration cubed.
visual_style: A RICE table assembling row by row, then a red alarm as bare moles rush toward the Kc expression — blocked by a gate labelled 'divide by volume' that stamps each value into a concentration.
mood: Checkpoint-thriller energy — the one gate every mark must pass through.
pacing: Brisk table build, sudden freeze at the gate, satisfying stamp-stamp-stamp release into the final answer.
call_to_action: Walk all seven chemistry questions at examination pace in the full practice run.
